which will include two coarse screen and grit removal trains, a SAFE system box, and two parallel fine screens

Screened effluent and return activated sludge will flow into two biological nutrient removal (BNR) basins and then pumped to the MBR. The BNR-MBR basins will be configured as two parallel activated sludge treatment trains, each consisting of pre-anoxic, aerobic, and post-anoxic basins in-series.

Filtrate from the MBR will be stored in two RO feed tanks, which will provide water for onsite uses and feed water to the RO system
Tertiary treated effluent from the outfall balancing tank will be pumped through an outfall disinfection chlorine contact pipeline
will then be dechlorinated by sodium bisulfite injection prior to discharge through the ocean outfall

A concrete tank, called the SAFE settling basin, will capture and equalize the wet weather flows prior to entering the SAFE filter system...the SAFE settling basin, which will provide sedimentation treatment
flows to the SAFE filter system for filtration treatment

RO concentrate will also be diverted directly to the RO concentrate disinfection contact pipeline for chlorination prior to commingling with the outfall disinfection contact pipeline
The sludge holding tanks will receive, store, and aerate activated sludge wasted from the BNR MBR process.
The sludge dewatering system will pump waste sludge from the sludge holding tanks, or directly from the MBR system, and dewatered by a belt filter press with a polymer storage and feed system.
Dewatered biosolids will be transported offsite for beneficial use or landfill.
